criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given a virtual meeting recording, when the system ingests the audio, then it should be available for transcription.
Given a non-supported audio format, when the system attempts ingestion, then it should reject the file with an error message.
Trust: The system logs the source of the audio file.

stories.notes: Ingested recordings now carry downloadUrl so transcription has a real fetch target, not just a validated-then-discarded field.

criteria.text: Given a physical meeting recording, when the system ingests the audio, then it should be available for transcription.
Given a noisy recording, when the system ingests the audio, then it should flag the segment for low confidence.
Trust: The system logs the source of the audio file.
Given a physical audio segment with crosstalk, when the system processes it, then it should flag it for low confidence.
Given a clear audio segment, when the system processes it, then it should not flag it for low confidence.
Trust: The system logs flagged segments for review.

stories.notes: Crosstalk detection is a stereo channel-overlap heuristic (real signal math), not diarization; mono recordings fall back to STORY-002's existing silence/clipping check. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001/STORY-002 — no explicit per-story value in plan.json.

criteria.text: Given a virtual meeting recording, when the system processes it, then it should tag the output with [Virtual — Platform].
Given a physical meeting recording, when the system processes it, then it should tag the output with [In-Person — Location].
Trust: The system logs the tagging information.

stories.notes: Physical ingestion gained a new optional 'location' input (nothing captured a room/site name before this story). No location supplied falls back to an honest 'Location unknown' placeholder rather than fabricating one. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001/002/003 — no explicit per-story value in plan.json.

criteria.text: Given an audio file, when the system transcribes it, then each line of text should have an associated timestamp.
Given a corrupted audio file, when the system attempts transcription, then it should fail gracefully with an error message.
Trust: The system logs transcription attempts and results.

stories.notes: Recorded from local verification (tsc --noEmit clean; 135/135 jest tests passing across 15 suites), not from an automated portal check. No real speech-to-text provider is wired in yet (TranscriptionClient is the seam for one); no HTTP route added either, since acceptance criteria don't require one. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001-004 — no explicit per-story value in plan.json.

criteria.text: Given an attendee list, when the system processes the audio, then it should map speakers to real names.
Given no attendee list, when the system processes the audio, then it should label speakers as 'Unidentified Speaker'.
Trust: The system logs speaker mapping attempts and results.
Given an inaudible segment, when the system processes it, then it should mark it as [inaudible].
Given a clear segment, when the system processes it, then it should not mark it as [inaudible].
Trust: The system logs marked segments for review.

stories.notes: Recorded from local verification (tsc --noEmit clean; 151/151 jest tests passing across 17 suites), not from an automated portal check. Confidence bands only activate once a real transcription provider reports per-segment confidence (none is wired in yet, same gap STORY-005 left open); the empty-text signal is the only one proven against realistic (non-synthetic) provider behavior today. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001-006 - no explicit per-story value in plan.json.

criteria.text: Given a transcribed meeting, when the system generates the summary, then it should include title, date, time, format, platform/location, attendees, and objective.
Given missing information, when the system generates the summary, then it should flag the missing fields for manual input.
Trust: The system logs summary generation attempts and results.

stories.notes: Recorded from local verification (tsc --noEmit clean; 157/157 jest tests passing across 18 suites), not from an automated portal check. Title and objective have no data source anywhere yet (no calendar-invite ingestion story exists) so they're caller-supplied via a new optional MeetingContext and flagged missing when absent. The other five fields reuse IngestedAudio.outputTag, the Attendee[] list STORY-006 accepts, and IngestedAudio.ingestedAt as a date/time fallback. The 'summary generation timeout' failure path (SummaryGenerationTimeoutError) is real, reachable code but not independently testable today, since synchronous assembly always resolves before the timeout timer can fire - documented in the test file rather than faked. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001-007 - no explicit per-story value in plan.json.

criteria.text: Given a transcribed meeting, when the system summarizes discussion points, then it should group them by topic with timestamp references.
Given unclear discussion points, when the system summarizes them, then it should flag them for review.
Trust: The system logs discussion point summaries and flags.

stories.notes: Recorded from local verification (tsc --noEmit clean; 164/164 jest tests passing across 19 suites), not from an automated portal check. Topic grouping/summarization is delegated to an injectable TopicSummarizationClient provider seam - the same governance boundary STORY-005/006 drew for TranscriptionClient/DiarizationClient - since no heuristic in this codebase can honestly group transcript text into topics; no real provider is wired in yet. Review-flagging reuses STORY-007's MarkedSegment.audibility rather than re-deriving it. The provider's returned topic ranges are validated for full, contiguous, in-order coverage of the transcript before being trusted, which is what makes 'incorrect topic grouping' a real, testable failure path (IncorrectTopicGroupingError) rather than blind trust in the response. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001-008 - no explicit per-story value in plan.json.

criteria.text: Given a transcribed meeting, when the system lists decisions, then each decision should include rationale and approver with a timestamp.
Given missing decision information, when the system lists decisions, then it should flag the missing fields for review.
Trust: The system logs decision listing attempts and results.

stories.notes: Recorded from local verification (tsc --noEmit clean; 171/171 jest tests passing across 20 suites), not from an automated portal check. Decision extraction is delegated to an injectable DecisionExtractionClient provider seam - the same governance boundary STORY-005/006 drew for TranscriptionClient/DiarizationClient and STORY-009 drew for TopicSummarizationClient - since no heuristic in this codebase can honestly extract decisions from transcript text; no real provider is wired in yet. A decision missing rationale/approver/timestamp is listed anyway with the gaps named in missingFields and flaggedForReview set true, satisfying the flag-for-review criterion literally rather than rejecting the whole listing. The provider response is validated (array shape, in-range timestamps) before being trusted, which is what makes incorrect decision listing a real, testable failure path (IncorrectDecisionListingError) rather than blind trust in the response. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001-009 - no explicit per-story value in plan.json.

criteria.text: Given a transcribed meeting, when the system extracts action items, then it should populate the table with owner, due date, priority, status, and source timestamp.
Given unclear action items, when the system extracts them, then it should flag them for review.
Trust: The system logs action item extraction attempts and results.

stories.notes: Recorded from local verification (tsc --noEmit clean; 179/179 jest tests passing across 21 suites), not from an automated portal check. Action item extraction is delegated to an injectable ActionItemExtractionClient provider seam - the same governance boundary STORY-005/006 drew for TranscriptionClient/DiarizationClient and STORY-009/010 drew for TopicSummarizationClient/DecisionExtractionClient - since no heuristic in this codebase can honestly extract action items from transcript text; no real provider is wired in yet. An action item missing owner/dueDate/priority/status/sourceTimestampMs is listed anyway with the gaps named in missingFields and flaggedForReview set true, satisfying the flag-for-review criterion literally rather than rejecting the whole item. The provider response is validated (array shape, priority/status enum values, in-range timestamps) before being trusted, which is what makes incorrect action item extraction a real, testable failure path (IncorrectActionItemExtractionError) rather than blind trust in the response. This entry corrects a pre-existing stale flag: criteria[].passed had already been set to true in the uncommitted working tree before any code for this story existed - flagged to the user at session start, now grounded in the real verification above. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001-010 - no explicit per-story value in plan.json.

Given requested edits, when the system receives them, then it should revise and re-present the draft for review.
Trust: The system logs review gate interactions and approvals.

criteria.text: Given approved draft minutes, when the system drafts emails, then each participant should receive an individualized email with their action items.
Given a participant with no action items, when the system drafts emails, then it should state 'No action items assigned to you from this meeting.'
Trust: The system logs email drafting attempts and results.

stories.notes: Recorded from local verification (tsc --noEmit clean; 215/215 jest tests passing across 24 suites), not from an automated portal check. draftEmails() calls reviewGate's assertApprovedForEmailDrafting (STORY-012's Gate #1 seam) before drafting anything, so drafting minutes that were never approved is structurally impossible, not just documented. Each attendee gets one email with the shared discussion topics/decisions plus only their own action items (case-insensitive owner match); an attendee with none gets the exact required sentence, verified with a literal string match. An action item whose owner matches no attendee is not attached to any email - it is surfaced in a batch-level unmatchedActionItems list with flaggedForReview true, satisfying the 'incorrect email personalization' failure path without silently dropping or misattaching it. This entry corrects a pre-existing stale flag: criteria[].passed had already been set to true in the uncommitted working tree before any code for this story existed - flagged to the user at session start, same pattern already caught and corrected for STORY-011 - now grounded in the real verification above. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001-011.

criteria.text: Given drafted emails, when the system presents them for review, then it should wait for explicit approval before sending.
Given requested adjustments, when the system receives them, then it should revise and re-present the emails for review.
Trust: The system logs review gate interactions and approvals.

stories.notes: Recorded from local verification (tsc --noEmit clean; 234/234 jest tests passing across 25 suites, 19 new), not from an automated portal check. Mirrors STORY-012's Gate #1 shape 1:1 but keyed on EmailDraftBatch (STORY-013's output) instead of DraftMinutes. assertApprovedForSending is the seam a future Email Delivery Service must call before dispatching any mail - it throws SendingNotApprovedError while pending and SessionNotFoundError when never submitted, so sending past an unapproved batch is structurally impossible, not just documented. requestRevision applies a caller-supplied revisedBatch and returns the session straight to pending_review in one action (no separate 'revision requested' state), satisfying the 'revise and re-present' criterion; a revised batch for the wrong session is rejected with ContractViolationError rather than silently misattached, covering the 'incorrect handling of requested adjustments' failure path. Every submit/revise/approve/blocked-check is written to the audit trail (service: 'reviewGateSending'), verified by a test asserting distinct auditEventIds and the correct error_class on a blocked check. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001-013.

criteria.text: Given email send confirmation, when the system logs action items, then each item should have a status of 'Not Started'.
Given a logging failure, when the system attempts to log action items, then it should retry and notify the user.
Trust: The system logs action item logging attempts and results.

stories.notes: Recorded from local verification (tsc --noEmit clean; 243/243 jest tests passing across 26 suites, 9 new), not from an automated portal check. logActionItems() verifies a caller-supplied EmailSendConfirmation against STORY-014's assertApprovedForSending before trusting it, then logs every action item from the approved batch (per-participant + unmatched) with status: 'Not Started' through an injectable ActionItemTrackerClient (no real tracker system wired in yet, same governance boundary every other provider seam in this project draws) wrapped in withTimeoutAndRetry. Deliberately uses the default retry-everything policy rather than the UpstreamTimeoutError-only precedent other stories set, since the acceptance criterion requires any logging failure to retry, not only a hung call. On exhausted retries an injectable notifyUserOfFailure hook fires (defaults to a structured audit event, since no real notification channel exists in this project yet) before ActionItemLoggingFailedError is thrown. Trust criterion verified via a real console.log/console.error spy test asserting distinct auditEventIds across a success and a failed+notified run. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001-014.

criteria.text: Given recurring meetings, when the system compares open items, then it should flag items open for more than 2 weeks.
Given no stale items, when the system compares open items, then it should confirm all items are current.
Trust: The system logs stale item flagging attempts and results.

stories.notes: Recorded from local verification (tsc --noEmit clean; 251/251 jest tests passing across 27 suites, 9 new), not from an automated portal check. compareOpenItems() matches items across two occurrences of a recurring meeting by (task, owner) case-insensitive, ages each current item from the earliest loggedAt seen across the prior and current lists, and flags anything open more than 14 days as 'Stale'; an exactly-14-day item is verified to stay 'Not Started' since the criterion is 'more than 2 weeks'. No persistent store of prior open items exists yet in this project, so the prior list is caller-supplied rather than queried - same provider-seam governance boundary STORY-005/006/009/010/011/015 already drew. Trust criterion verified via a real console.log/console.error spy test asserting stale_item_comparison_attempted -> stale_items_flagged/all_items_current/stale_item_comparison_failed, all with distinct auditEventIds. This entry corrects a pre-existing stale flag: criteria[].passed had already been flipped to true in the uncommitted working tree at session start, before any code for this story existed - flagged to the user at session start, same pattern already caught and corrected for STORY-006/007/008/011/013/015 - now grounded in the real verification above. points_awarded assumes 8/criterion, same convention as STORY-001-015.
